cards.text: Israel is camped at the foot of Mount Sinai, and the mountain is wrapped in smoke and quaking. Moses, Israel's leader, has gone down to the people. And then God speaks all these words.

cards.question: Before a single command, God tells Israel who He is. He's the LORD their God who did what?

cards.text: No warm-up, no small talk, no "so how's everybody doing?" God opens with who got them OUT, out of the land of Egypt and out of the house of slavery.

cards.question: Then comes the first command. Since He's the LORD their God, what does He tell Israel?

answers.text: Have no other gods before Him
Build Him an altar on the mountain
Bring Him an offering each morning

cards.question: God tells Israel not to make an ___ in the form of anything in the heavens, on the earth or in the waters.

cards.text: And it's not just about making them, because God says don't bow down to them or worship them either.

cards.question: God gives a reason Israel must not bow down to idols. What kind of God does He call Himself?

cards.text: Then God sets two things side by side. For those who hate Him, the iniquity of the fathers is visited on their children to the third and fourth generations.

cards.question: For those who love God and keep His commandments, He shows loving devotion to a thousand generations.

cards.text: Three or four generations on one side, a THOUSAND on the other. Friend, that's not a close game, that's a scoreboard reading four to a thousand.

cards.question: God says He will leave unpunished anyone who takes His name in vain.

cards.text: Next, God puts a day on the calendar: "Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy." Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, trust me, being REMEMBERED is a big deal.

cards.question: Six days are for labor. Then the ___ day is a Sabbath to the LORD, with no ___ at all.
The Sabbath rest God commands even covers Israel's livestock.

cards.text: Livestock included, so even the cows get a day off! I worked every birthday and holiday the Millers ever had with no Sabbath, but after years in a drawer I figure I'm caught up through about the year three thousand.

cards.question: God gives Israel a reason for the Sabbath. What is it?

answers.text: He made everything in six days and rested on the seventh
Israel rested for seven days after leaving Egypt
Moses waited seven days at the foot of the mountain

cards.text: That's why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy. He set the pattern Himself, way back at creation.
The next command starts at home. God says to honor your father and mother, and this one comes with a promise.

cards.question: What does God promise to those who honor their father and mother?

answers.text: Long days in the land God is giving them
A double share of their father's land
Many sons to carry on their name

cards.text: Then the commands get REAL short, no speeches, just BAM: "You shall not murder." BAM: "You shall not commit adultery."

cards.question: Another short command, just four words: You shall not ___.
Next, God gives Israel a command about their neighbor. What is it?

answers.text: Do not bear false witness against him
Do not lend to him for profit
Do not move his boundary stone

cards.text: One more: "You shall not covet your neighbor’s house." And God keeps going with his wife, his servants, his ox and his donkey.

cards.question: After the house, the wife, the servants, the ox and the donkey, God adds one last thing: do not covet ___ that belongs to your ___.

cards.text: ANYTHING, so every loophole is closed. Nobody gets to stand there going, "Well, TECHNICALLY, it was his goat."
Now look at the scene the people are standing in: thunder, lightning, the ram's horn sounding and the mountain wrapped in smoke.

cards.question: Seeing the thunder, the lightning and the smoke, the people rush closer to the mountain.
The people go to Moses with a request. What do they ask?

answers.text: That Moses speak to them instead of God
That Moses take them back to Egypt
That Moses lead them away from Sinai

cards.text: Their words: "But do not let God speak to us, or we will die." I get it, friend, because back in the drawer we all held our breath every time the light came in, and that was just a KITCHEN light.

cards.question: Moses tells the people not to be afraid.
Moses says God has come to test the people, so the fear of Him will keep them from ___.
While the people stand at a distance, Moses stays back with them.

cards.text: The people stay back, and Moses approaches the thick darkness where God was. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this conversation on the mountain isn't over.

findings.problem: This story card mostly restates the answer card 2 just gave (God brought them out of Egypt). The only new detail is 'the house of slavery,' so the card repeats instead of moving the passage forward.
This card retells the contrast cards 8 and 9 already covered (third and fourth generations against a thousand) and adds a scoreboard joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card restates card 14's answer ('Livestock included') and then only jokes. It tells no new part of the passage. Exodus 20:10 also names the son, the daughter, the servants and the foreigner within the gates, and the card could carry that detail instead.

The Sabbath cards never mention the foreigner within your gates, the son and daughter, or the servants, all of whom Exodus 20:10 includes in the rest. The fact that even the foreigner is covered is a key detail for understanding the command.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'I worked every birthday and holiday the Millers ever had with no Sabbath' adds a new claim to his backstory. It says he worked with no rest at all in the Millers' kitchen. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, not new facts about the Millers' kitchen.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'You shall not ___' with no context is guessing the next word of a short line. The card gives nothing to reason from, such as what the command protects.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 6 quotes 'You shall not covet your neighbor’s house' and lists 'his wife, his servants, his ox and his donkey.' That gives away the second blank, 'neighbor,' before card 7 asks for it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card restates card 7's answer ('ANYTHING') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.
The punchline 'Well, TECHNICALLY, it was his goat' doesn't land as a loophole. It isn't clear who is speaking or why a goat would be an excuse, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line copies the doc's example phrase word for word: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
